newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP keen to resolve Foster's stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP keen to resolve Foster's stake.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said it was actively looking at realising its investment in Foster's Brewing Group Ltd but could not say if this would be achieved by the end of the resource giant's financial year on May 31.

BHP, which counts minerals, copper, petroleum and steel as its main operating divisions, has a 37 percent stake in Australia's largest brewer. It has been a rumoured seller of the stake for the last year or so.

"As for whether there's some other way of capturing value from the investment in Foster's, that's something that we're certainly more actively looking at than perhaps we were last year," BHP chief executive John Prescott said in an interview on Channel Nine.
Prescott also said BHP had made its own inquiries about what to do with its investment since his last interview on the programme in February this year.
"We've had more approaches and we've made more inquiries that's all I can say," he said.

"And there's been more speculation on what we might do and the value of the shares has continued to rise, maybe not the last week or two but if you take it over three months, it's continued to rise," Prescott said.
BHP's investment in Foster's was valued at A$1.85 billion based on the brewer's closing price of A$2.55 on Friday.
International brewers such as Canada's Molson Cos Ltd, Philip Morris and Holland's Heineken have been mooted as possible buyers, analysts have said.

BHP acquired its Foster's stake in the late 1980s, a period when the mining giant was under takeover threat from Robert Holmes a Court and the company found an unusual ally in the form of former Foster's owner Elders IXL Ltd.
